issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), and the template/Main references Milkable. However, the solution implementation introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (with messageOnMilk()) and has an empty Milkable.java file. Several concrete classes (Goat, Seal) implement Dairy instead of Milkable. This type/name mismatch between 'Milkable' (specified) and 'Dairy' (implemented) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and can prevent successful compilation or correct integration with tests that expect a 'Milkable' interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by using the interface name 'Milkable' everywhere. Either rename Dairy.java to Milkable.java (and ensure it declares messageOnMilk()), remove the empty Milkable.java file, and make Goat and Seal implement Milkable; or change the problem statement/UML and template to consistently use 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable'. The simplest fix: replace Dairy with Milkable in the solution, delete the empty Milkable.java file, and ensure all classes and imports reference Milkable.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution introduces an interface named 'Dairy' and has animal classes implement 'Dairy' instead. Additionally the solution contains an empty Milkable.java file. This name mismatch (Milkable vs Dairy) breaks the conceptual mapping between the exercise description/UML and the provided solution/template and will confuse students about which interface they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update its filename to Milkable.java) and update Seal and Goat to implement Milkable. Remove the redundant/empty Milkable.java file if present or consolidate it so there's only one Milkable interface matching the problem statement and UML.
